items.title: Second Officer Tells Francique Inquest Surveillance, Not a Planned Arrest, Was Underway That Night
items.summary: According to testimony at the coroner's inquest into the death of Jamal Francique, Det. Mani Sharifi said police had no plan to arrest Francique on the night he was fatally shot in 2020. Sharifi told the inquest officers moved in only after they observed Francique breaching his bail conditions by leaving his home. The real plan, Sharifi said, was to continue surveillance that had already been underway for roughly three or four days until an opportunity arose. A juror asked why Francique was not arrested earlier in the week, once officers first saw him breach his bail, and Sharifi said his unit was instead focused on investigating whether Francique possessed a firearm or was involved in drug activity. Francique was shot by an officer outside a Mississauga townhouse complex on the evening of Jan. 7, 2020, according to the inquest.

items.title: Mississauga Ward 10 Councillor to Host Virtual Town Hall on Lisgar Beaver Problem
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga Ward 10 Coun. Sue McFadden says the city will hold a virtual town hall on Jan. 13 to explain its strategy for managing beavers disrupting water flow in the city's northwest end. Officials plan to outline efforts to keep the animals from causing further problems in the Lisgar community, near the Milton border. The city removed several beaver dams and relocated beavers from around Sixteen Mile Creek and Osprey Marsh last fall and winter after the dams caused drainage issues, according to the report. Despite that removal effort, residents reported seeing beavers back in the area by spring, prompting McFadden to promise closer monitoring. McFadden says beavers, among the largest rodents in the world, continue to live along Sixteen Mile Creek, and another lodge and series of dams have recently been spotted further north within the tributary.

items.title: Helicopter Tracks Driver Going Over 200 km/h Through Mississauga and Brampton to an Arrest
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police, a driver was clocked travelling more than 200 km/h on Mississauga and Brampton streets and highways in an incident officers tied to the recent release of Grand Theft Auto VI. Police released video showing the vehicle speeding through both cities before reaching the highway, say officers. Air3, the force's helicopter unit, tracked the vehicle from above until officers located it at a residence and made an arrest, police say. Peel police used the stop as what they called a cheeky example of what not to do on the roads, reminding residents that unlike the video game, there are no respawns or reset buttons in real life. Officers say the message was simple, keep the speeding, stunts and getaway drives in the game, not on Mississauga's roads.

items.title: Rising Complaints Across Peel Push Public Health Review to Call for More Inspectors
items.summary: According to a Peel Public Health review, the region needs to hire more public health inspectors in the coming year to keep up with rising complaints and meet Ontario guidelines. The review found food safety complaints and service requests in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon rose 23 per cent from 2024 to 2025, while special events requiring inspection increased 22 per cent over the same period. Peel employed at least 43 public health inspectors in 2025, with a median salary of $103,376, according to the Ontario Sunshine List. Those inspectors cover retail food, personal service settings, child care centres, recreational water and tanning facilities, and tobacco and vaping retailers, rated under a green, yellow and red system. The staffing shortage means inspections are increasingly delayed or missed, the review says, raising the risk of foodborne illness and other preventable incidents.

items.title: Elementary Students Across Peel Region Get a Professional Activity Day on Nov. 27
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, elementary students in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon will get a three day weekend this month because of a Professional Activity Day. Both the Peel District School Board and the Dufferin-Peel Catholic District School Board have scheduled the PA day for Nov. 27, giving families extra time to prepare for the holiday season. The day off applies only to elementary students, according to the boards' official school year calendars. Secondary students at both boards will get their next PA day later, on Wednesday, Feb. 3. Families can use the extra day to get a head start on holiday plans or a visit with Santa at the mall, the outlet notes.

items.title: Project Sega Investigation Leads to Charges in String of Employment Agency Robberies
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police, two Brampton men have been charged following a string of armed robberies at employment agencies across Mississauga and Brampton between April and August. Police say masked suspects entered the businesses and confronted employees at gunpoint, with knives also used in some incidents, stealing cash, gift cards, electronic devices and other property. The robberies resulted in losses exceeding $53,000, according to police. Investigators identified the pair through a probe called Project Sega and seized a stolen vehicle worth roughly $30,000 along with two replica firearms, police say. Satnam Dhillon, 31, and Rajdeep Singh, 21, both of Brampton, were arrested and charged with multiple counts of robbery and disguise with intent, and Dhillon faces additional charges including fail to comply with a release order.

items.title: Second Victim Comes Forward a Year After Mississauga Massage Therapist's Arrest, Halton Police Say
items.summary: According to Halton police, a 53 year old Mississauga man working as a registered massage therapist has been charged with a second count of sexual assault after an additional victim came forward. Police say the man was first arrested on Nov. 19 following an investigation that began in October into an allegation that a woman was sexually assaulted in May 2025. The suspect worked as a registered massage therapist at Massage Addict in Milton, according to police. He now faces one count of sexual assault tied to the original complaint and a second charge stemming from the newly reported incident, police say. Halton police say the latest charge came roughly a year after the man's initial arrest, when a second complainant came forward.

items.title: Shuttle Buses Fill In at Pearson Airport as Maintenance Cuts Automated Train Service to One Line
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Toronto Pearson Airport's Terminal Link train is running on a single track this week while crews carry out routine maintenance work. Airport officials say only one of the two fully automated, driverless trains is operating, with the reduced service taking effect early this week and continuing into next week. Shuttle buses are filling in between Terminal 1, Terminal 3 and Viscount Station while the second train is down, the airport says. The free trains normally link travellers to the Sheraton Gateway Hotel, the ALT Hotel and the Value Park garage and lot, officials note. When running at full capacity, the Terminal Link operates around the clock, with trips between stations typically taking two to eight minutes, according to the airport. Officials describe the temporary reduction as part of planned work meant to keep the line operating safely and reliably.

items.title: Arrest Made in Fatal Toronto Shooting of Mississauga Man, Second Suspect Still Wanted
items.summary: According to insauga.com, police have arrested one of two suspects wanted in the fatal shooting of a Mississauga man in Toronto. Officers found the victim with gunshot wounds on Saturday, Nov. 7 and performed life-saving measures before paramedics took him to hospital, where he died, making him Toronto's 33rd homicide victim of 2026. Police identified two suspects on Nov. 14 and issued Canada-wide warrants for Armani Callender, 19, and Cameron Marlor, 17, both of Toronto. On Sunday, Nov. 22, Toronto police announced they had arrested and charged Callender. He faces charges of second-degree murder, attempted murder, possession of a firearm while not holding a licence, and possession of a loaded regulated firearm. Marlor, the second suspect, remains outstanding, police say.
